framing_issues.text: Each district or school also picks its start date, up to July 1, 2027.
framing_issues.issue: Missing context and internal inconsistency. Line 21 says the law doesn't say how the Jan 1 policy deadline (P-008: policies that prohibit K-12 access, first due Jan 1, 2027) fits with the July 1, 2027 start (P-007). Lines 14, 22, 27 and 31 still present a free choice of start date up to July 1, 2027 as settled. A family could plan around July 2027 when its district's January policy already covers high school.

framing_issues.text: HB 1009 leaves that rule as it was.
framing_issues.issue: Missing context for K-8 families: the bill drops e-readers from the device examples the K-8 rule uses (P-021 vs P-004) and makes the policy deadline yearly for all grades (P-020 vs P-008).

framing_issues.text: No one in the sources we reviewed disputed that the rules work.
framing_issues.issue: A "no one disputes" claim that leaves out the English study's authors, who said their findings don't support school phone bans "in their current form" and that such policies "require further development" (P-043). Limit it to Georgia, or mention P-043.

framing_issues.text: If you care most about reaching your child in an emergency
framing_issues.issue: The values guide ties emergency contact only to opposing the ban. Yet 60.3% of supporting parents cited "Improved physical health and safety" (P-034), and Gazmararian says policies can address emergency access (P-037). Readers may infer that caring about safety means opposing. A note that safety appears on both sides would fix this.

framing_issues.text: Sen. Sally Harrell said legislators want to hear teachers say, "I can just teach again."
framing_issues.issue: Placed under "Who disagrees" as a counter to Adams. But it says what legislators want to hear (P-045), not that teachers have said it, so readers may take it as teacher testimony.
"All-day" can read as round-the-clock; the source says "bell-to-bell" (the school day). Same wording at line 177.

framing_issues.text: In the English study, strict rules went with about 40 minutes less phone time
framing_issues.issue: Listed under "What supports it" on the mental-health and friendships card, though the same study found no well-being difference (P-042, P-043). Less phone time during school is not itself evidence for the card's claim.

framing_issues.text: A student may access a device that their IEP, Section 504 plan or medical plan explicitly requires.
framing_issues.issue: Unexplained term: "IEP" is first used here but spelled out only at line 79. Expand it as "IEP (Individualized Education Program)" at first use.
Vague reference: when this first sentence appears alone on the home page, "these students" has no referent unless the label is shown with it.

framing_issues.text: you can ask your questions there
framing_issues.issue: P-060 says these events are "designed to promote distraction-free education". Presenting them as a place to raise policy questions leaves out that purpose.

framing_issues.text: Gov. Brian Kemp said the bills he signed would "reduce distractions in the classroom."
framing_issues.issue: The quote covers several bills signed that day (P-029), so it is thin support for this card. The wording "the bills he signed" is accurate, but readers may take it as being about HB 1009 alone.

framing_issues.text: The Georgia Department of Education must give schools guidance and technical support.
framing_issues.issue: Listed under "Coming up" with no date. The law sets none, and the line could say so.

framing_issues.text: The same goes for suspensions and for reaching students in an emergency.
